inference_protocol: Video IDs identify the normalized input clips/views and must never be inferred from event or slot IDs.
A reasoning cycle is PLAN -> local FOCUS observation -> memory revision; Reasoner ALIGN may then rebuild the evidence synthesis when useful. Completing one cycle does not imply sufficient evidence.
FOCUS evidence is valid only for its cited video and time span; it cannot prove whole-video or cross-video absence.
Count physical entities or transitions, not frames, mentions, or duplicate observations of the same event.
The final answer must be exactly one option label from the supplied choices, never a video ID, option text, refusal, or unknown.
If evidence remains incomplete when no executable visual budget remains, choose the best-supported option label and retain the uncertainty in the summary.

findings.statement: v1 evidence shows grey-part handling against a blue body, screwdriver use, interior installation, and later unscrewing/manipulation of a black chassis, but current evidence does not identify any v1 action as functionally unnecessary.
v2 evidence shows dark chassis/device manipulation with a screwdriver, but current evidence does not directly show body/chassis separation or establish that such separation was unnecessary.

v3 evidence shows a black internal component held separately from the blue chassis and inserted into it, plus screwdriver work on the exposed component and rotation revealing wheels; the functional necessity of the separation/insertion is not established.
v3 fine focus shows screwdriver work on the side of the black internal component, a pause, and an attempted manual screw insertion, but the purpose of these actions is not visible.
v3 evidence also shows wheel attachment to a blue car body and a final held assembled body with wheels nearby, but this does not prove the wheel attachment was unnecessary.

open_questions.question: Whether the v1 grey-part handling was functionally unnecessary remains unresolved.
Whether the observed v2 chassis/device manipulation involved an unnecessary separation remains unresolved.
Whether the v3 black internal component separation/insertion or screwdriver access was functionally unnecessary remains unresolved.
Whether the v3 wheel attachment was functionally unnecessary given the observed assembly state remains unresolved.
